# Theory
<!-- {{< include sections/lab1_theory.qmd >}} -->

## Why can it be important to consider various probability thresholds in the classification problems?

Different classifcation threshholds (r) affect trade-off between false positives and false negatives. This can be particulary important when the consequences of the different classification errors are not equally severe. For example, lowering the threshold in disease detection can identify more patients with the disease, but at the cost of more false positives.

The textbook show example of this on page 92-93, example 4.5. It compares a default threshold of 0.5 with 0.15 for detecting thyroid disease.


## What ways of collecting correct values of the target variable for the supervised learning problems are mentioned in the book? 

## How can one express the cost function of the linear regression in the matrix form, according to the book?

The cost function for linear regression with squared error loss can be expressed in matrix form as,

$$
J(\boldsymbol{\theta})
= \frac{1}{n}\|X\boldsymbol{\theta}-\mathbf{y}\|_2^2,
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\theta}$ is the
vector of regression coefficients, $\mathbf{y}$ is the vector
of observed responses, and $n$ is the number of observations.
The cost function represents the mean squared error between
the predicted and observed values and is minimized when
estimating the regression coefficients.

The textbook show this on page 45, equation (3.11)
